bug_fixed_2026-09-07.description: Found via carrier/lift/harness/GCC_X87.md SS4: line_intersect's ua/ub NaN guards (D==0 && numerator==0, i.e. segments sharing their start point) were written as `if (!(ua >= 0.0)) return 0;` / `if (!(ub >= 0.0)) return 0;`, which reject on NaN because `NaN >= 0.0` is false and the negation is true. The original x87 code's fucom/fnstsw/test $0x45,%ah/je idiom only branches on the ORDERED true case, so a NaN ua/ub falls through every guard uncaught; the original then runs a masked fistp on NaN+0.5 (integer indefinite 0x80000000), writes garbage coordinates, and returns EAX=1, whereas the un-fixed source returned EAX=0 on those vectors -- a toolchain-independent mismatch (948-1011 of every 20000 vectors, identical across every MSVC and GCC build tried, unrelated to floating-point precision).
